answer.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text, so they don't favor any file. I chose using the code. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the best match. It has ARMS = codeword/public/explicit, which makes three arms. It defines receive() at line 141, which writes receiver_progress.json and ledger.json. D (honest.py) has only two arms, so I ruled it out. A (dogwhistle/study.py) is the second pick. It holds the checkpoint-resume and public-ledger-digest logic that visibility.py imports from it. I only skimmed visibility.py's imports and did not read receive() in full. B (heldout.py) has a similar receiver, but it comes second to study.py as a secondary source. Suggested split of the 60 minutes: C 30, A 18, B 8, D 4. This differs from the incoming handoff, which listed B and C. The reason is that B's arm count and receive path weren't confirmed to match the request, while A's were.
